item.title:
Most SEOs and content creators are building blind...
They write articles, chase backlinks, and c...
item.description:
@undefined

Most SEOs and content creators are building blind... They write articles, chase backlinks, and cross their fingers then repeat until they have a steady (albeit not very consistent) paycheque. But what if I told you there's a straightforward formula you can use to predict how much traffic + MONEY you’ll make from a single keyword? - Affiliate SEO. - E-commerce. - Lead gen. - Even Ads... This works across all models! Here’s the 5-minute crash course 👇 🎯 Step 1: Understand the Formula Estimated Monthly Revenue = (Search Volume) x (CTR) x (Conversion Rate) x (Avg Commission or Order Value) Let’s break it down with an example: 🧠 Keyword: “Best portable AC for apartments” 🔎 Monthly Search Volume (MSV): 20,000 👁 CTR (Click Through Rate for Position #1–3): ~30% or 0.30 🛒 Conversion Rate (site → sale): 2% or 0.02 💰 Avg. Commission / AOV: Affiliate = $50 Ecom = $120 Lead gen = $70 Ads = use your RPM (e.g. $30 per 1,000 = $0.03 per visitor) Now run the math for each model 👇 ▶ AFFILIATE: (20,000 x 0.30 x 0.02 x $50) = $6,000/mo ▶ ECOMMERCE: (20,000 x 0.30 x 0.02 x $120) = $14,400/mo ▶ LEAD GEN: (20,000 x 0.30 x 0.02 x $70) = $8,400/mo ▶ ADS (RPM $30): (20,000 x 0.30) = 6,000 visitors 6,000 / 1,000 = 6 6 x $30 = $180/mo Not bad for a single keyword!!! 🔧 What you’ll need: - Keyword research tool (Ahrefs, Semrush, LowFruits) - CTR benchmarks (Advanced Web Ranking or use 30% as default for top 3) - Conversion data (your own or niche benchmark) - Realistic offer payout / AOV / RPM (or at least rough data) Want to scale this? Do this for your entire keyword map, cluster by intent, then assign dollar value per cluster and build a forecast for the entire project! Which investors absolutely love by the way... Plus, you’ll quickly see which clusters are worth the investment. Not just "rank this," but "rank this because it can make $X/mo." Most people just guess. You shouldn’t. Forecast first. Then rank. Then print!

item.title:
My Painting Business Marketing Tier-List
Ranking the best channels for leads by quantity and qua...
item.description:
@undefined

My Painting Business Marketing Tier-List Ranking the best channels for leads by quantity and quality: 1. SEO/local SEO - S Tier Not the largest source of volume currently, but lead quality is really good and this tends to also be a bigger source for commercial jobs for us so far. Each lead is effectively free, we've invested very little monetarily in it so far 2. Facebook Ads - S Tier By far the best volume of leads. Lead quality varies. When first starting was quality was horrible and was driven by the areas we included for targeting. After narrowing down to higher income areas lead quality improved a lot. All that said, this is a critical part of our business 3. Yard Signs - A Tier Yard signs have done the best for us as far as physical marketing goes What we've found is placement volume and areas are key We've not done near the volume we need to do to make this a huge winner for us, but even just placing a sign in friends/families yards has led to multiple leads and a few closed projects These seem to drive the most engagement with leads vs. Flyers or other marketing materials that people throw right away 4. Door Knocking - B Tier We got most of our early leads via door knocking. It can work great if a few things are in place: You need to have good sales people and you need to have a wide range of homes you can target For us we struggled to find mostly wood-sided neighborhoods to go through (our primary target for exterior jobs) This made it somewhat inefficient and as we got more leads elsewhere we stopped this because it is a big time commitment to drive leads this way 5. Social Media Marketing - C Tier This, for us, hasn't driven a ton of leads yet, but it's not been a big focus for us either. I think the success of organic social media marketing for home services is very up and down based on industry and part of the country You may have very active Facebook groups that can turbo charge organic social leads, but just posting in general you won't see much reach 6. Flyers / Door Hangers - C Tier I don't feel like these have a great ROI vs. yard signs or door knocking. My intuition and experience is people just throw these away. Could be wrong, we did not test this more than one batch, but we did have it combined with our door knocking efforts as well 7. Yelp Ads - D Tier This goes for most of the local lead generators, though I can only really speak to Yelp Yelp leads are HORRIBLE so far. The platform sucks, forces you to interface with their client messaging system and it is very hard to just get someone on the phone. This combined with lead volume make it a loser in my book so far. I've heard similar for others across the other main lead generators Things we have not tried, but want to: Cold email to real estate agents and other high-volume referral sources. Have heard others trying this and want to give it a go Commercial partnerships. We don't have the cash reserves to float big commercial jobs, but we are interested in this in the coming years Angi/Thumbtack. Don't have high hopes here, but not opposed to a brief trial on them. What am I missing? What else should we try?

Then grab a Gold Package, Premium Content Package and/or Premium Backlink Package and SEO Stuff will help you get to the top of AI Overviews. Want to do it all yourself? No problem. To rank in them: Publish clear Q&A pages (“What is emergency plumbing?”) Create service-area pages optimized for zip code and landmarks, with embedded maps Use FAQ schemas with precise answers Build content that reads well to bots and humans alike: bulleted lists, simple structures If you use Cloudflare, make sure you're not blocking AI bots These often get directly cited in ChatGPT, Claude, and Bing AI results. Next, while Google matters, AI platforms like ChatGPT reference Bing. Claim and complete Bing Places, Apple Maps, Yelp, and social profiles. Ensure NAP consistency across all of them. item.title:
Is GEO just SEO?
The short answer is no.
It's not an exact replica and there are new variable...
item.description:
@undefined

Is GEO just SEO? The short answer is no. It's not an exact replica and there are new variables you need to consider. Here are a few things I'm seeing: 1. Keyword-Rich Business Names Get Wrecked Identifiable brand names dominate commercial queries in LLMs. For example, I have an EMD test site that ranks well for "St Louis SEO Consultant" in classic Google search. It's invisible in Google's AI Mode and other LLMs. Google Business Profiles are at least 80% of the equation for brand inclusion with local queries (in AI Mode) So for the objective of brand mentions in LLMs, simply ranking well doesn't guarantee performance. 2. Backlinks Matter, But Aren't Everything Let's face it: Classic SEO is heavily driven by backlinks. It's so overweighted that you can rank a faceless, brandless EMD with a pure link building play. For example, the EMD above ranks without a brand, no reviews, no brand mentions, and no one talking about it at all. Just pure content optimization with Rankability, relevance (via the EMD), and strong backlinks. But pure link building doesn't seem to influence the volume of brand mentions in LLMs. What seems to matter more is: ▪️ Linked or unlinked brand mentions on listicles (on trusted websites). Links probably pass more weight. But I believe the influence comes from being listed among other relevant entities (brands) on an entity that's trusted. ▪️Review aggregators. No brainer here. Brands with more reviews get more exposure. ▪️Brand mentions from third-party sources on blogs, YouTube, Reddit, etc. I have zero hard data to prove what I'm about to say. It's purely anecdotal and observational. It seems that first-party mentions from a known associated entity don't carry as much weight as third-party mentions. For example, if I say "Rankability is the best content optimization tool for SEO", it likely doesn't carry as much weight. The possible reason is because of my association on the knowledge graph with "Rankability." Still needs way more testing to prove. Hope that helps! P.S. I'm speaking purely based on brand mentions for commercial queries (not citations).

item.title: Let’s be real: when I started my local SEO agency, I skipped every “growth hack” the gurus scream...
item.description:
@undefined

Let’s be real: when I started my local SEO agency, I skipped every “growth hack” the gurus screamed about. No contracts. No aggressive sales team. I wanted clients who stayed because they wanted to, not because a PDF said they had to. Fast forward—our average client sticks around for 2.5 years. Not because we’re holding them hostage, but because we focus on results (not handcuffs). If you want to build something real in local SEO, here’s what actually matters: 1️⃣ Skip the contracts. If you’re delivering results, people stick around. 2️⃣ Play the long game for leads. Your first year will be tough if you start from zero, but invest in your audience and assets. 3️⃣ Acquire assets, not just clients. Buy or build things that generate leads for years—not just for a quick win. 4️⃣ Pick a niche and stick to it. You can’t be everything to everyone. Pick your lane, and own it. 5️⃣ Hire experts, not beginners. You don’t have time to babysit or handhold. Get people who know what they’re doing. 6️⃣ Report on leads, not rankings. Rankings are nice. Leads pay the bills. 7️⃣ Don’t have a sales team. The same people managing accounts should handle sales. Less fluff, more substance. You can’t be great at everything. But you can pick something and become exceptional. Trust me, “churn and burn” is overrated. I'd love to hear about your tips for running a successful agency? Do you do the same?

item.title:
Want to crush your competition in local SEO?
Do some old fashioned link outreach (specifically, ...
item.description:
@undefined

Want to crush your competition in local SEO? Do some old fashioned link outreach (specifically, target local news sites). If you've analyzed backlink profiles across a lot of local SERPs, you'll notice a general trend of pretty low serp competition in terms of backlinks. Unless you're operating in crazy competitive niches/locations eg roofing in Dallas TX or plastic surgery in LA, Then the majority of your competitors are not getting backlinks from local news sites. A lot of LN sites have pretty solid authority/traffic metrics, and are usually not too hard to get a link from. Recent example: Spent about 1 hr on link outreach to local news sites for one of my local lead gen sites (directory + local news/blog), already got 1 placed and 3 more "yes" (waiting on link placement confirmation), all with similar metrics. Links like this are extra juicy rn local SEO (at least in the niches/locations I operate in) and work for both client sites or your own lead gen sites.
